title.narrative: World Vision CORE Project fas II
World Vision CORE Project phase II

description.narrative: Projektet syftar till att öka möjligheten för produktiv sysselsättning utanför jordbruket, för ökad inkomst för kvinnor och unga i distrikten Nyamasheke och Rusizi. Detta genom att öka företagande och affärsverksamhet utanför jordbruket för målgruppen, genom förbättrat företagsklimat, ökad tillgång till finansiella tjänster samt informations- och kommunikationsteknologi. Särskilt fokus kommer att läggas på utveckling och av värdekedjor inom honungsproduktion och sömnad för att göra dem mer inkluderande av målgruppen.

The project aims to contribute to productive off-farm employment in order to increase household income for women and youth in Nyamasheke and Rusizi districts. The project contributes to increased off-farm entrepreneurship and market oriented businesses for the target group, through enhanced enabling environment for cooperatives and businesses, increased access to financial services and information and communication technologies. Special focus will be placed on developing the value chains in honey production and tailoring to make them more inclusive of for target group.

Examples of results under each outputs/outcome based on the annual narrative reports, follow-ups and final evaluation of the project.
Impact Level Increased household off-farm incomes for women and youth in Rusizi and Nyamasheke districts
In a post project survey, it was shown that the average monthly income of the beneficiaries was Rwf.50,000 after the intervention reflecting an increase from the initial average monthly income Rwf.24,856 for women and Rwf.22,944 for the youth. The qualitative data collected also shows a big change in behavior from those who participated in the project, where respondents highlight that they have changed their saving habits, personal financial management, power dynamics within the household relating to making key household financial decisions. The final evaluation also indicates that the beneficiaries reported improvements in their self-reliance and self-esteem due to their participation in the project interventions
Outcome 1 Increased off-farm entrepreneurship and market-oriented businesses among women and youth under outcome 1, the following results were achieved
Cooperative formation, registration, and capacity building 69% of the cooperatives engaged under the programme were supported to register their cooperatives under Rwanda Cooperatives Agency (RCA). The formation registration increased their possibilities to different opportunities including collective market access and increased cooperative revenues. The evaluation though highlights that the graduation of the Village Savings and Loan Associations (VSLAs) into either formal cooperatives or entrepreneurs was slow in comparison with the project target of 80% Increasing Access to Finance the project supported with formalization of the VSLAs, their graduation into formal cooperatives and SMEs, facilitating their access to finance by linking them to Savings and Credit Cooperatives (SACCOs), Micro Finance Institutions (MFIs) and Business Development Fund (BDF). Additionally, the project supported the establishment of revolving fund to increase access to seed funding for new business startups that traditionally would struggle to funding. The project managed to support over 25,000 and 11, 000 women and youth respectively to access loans from both formal and informal finance providers. The project also supported the target group with capacity building on financial education, even though only 21% were reached by the project (according to final evaluation), they indicated that the training was impactful. In relation to the VLSAs graduation, at least 34% of the cooperatives managed to graduate from VSLAs into formal cooperatives or formed their own Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs). Of those who graduated, the majority (52%) transitioned to entrepreneurship with 35% joined cooperatives. Enhancing participation of youth and women The final evaluation indicates that majority of these target groups participated in the project activities. For instance, by the end of the project, a total of 150 MSMEs were managed by Women and/ youth in comparison with the initial project target of 100 MSMEs. The initial project target on youth involvement in off-farm MSMEs was surpassed, whereby the end of the project, 3,999 youth were involved in off-farm MSMEs compared to 3,572 project target, while 6,260 women were involved in off-farm MSMEs compared to the project target of 9,469. Access and use of ICT4D with an aim to increase market access, the project supported the cooperatives and MSMEs in using ICT tools to enhance and improve their businesses. The project final evaluation indicates that, beneficiaries most especially the youth, used the acquired ICT knowledge to start their own business e.g., cyber cafes, others reported online presence of their business especially on social media platforms like Facebook and WhatsApp which increase their business visibility. This component also supported women and youth to use smartphones to keep track of their savings under the VSLAs. The figures from the log frame indicate that 4,396 youth and 4,043 women reported increased access to markets due to ICT4D services.
Outcome 2 Improved business competitiveness for tailoring and honey value chains under outcome 2, the following results were achieved;
MSD Capacity Building at least 88 stakeholders on Market Systems Development Approach. The project aimed to pilot an MSD approach to building the competitiveness of the tailoring and honey value chains. The approach is premised on the idea that well-functioning markets are the best way to deliver sustained and inclusive improvement in incomes, profits, and livelihoods. The final evaluation highlights that the project component was slightly weak as it couldn't provide indication of a) the quality of the training, b) the relevance of the capacity building & c) how the acquired skills were used to transform the market system and its actors. Onboarding of lead firms The project managed to link honey producers to two leading aggregators and processors of honey in Rwanda ABDC and Apiary. Similarly, the project successfully linked INEZA textiles to tailoring cooperatives Rusizi and Nyamasheke districts who them provided market for their products Linking MSMEs and cooperatives to lead firms By the end of the project, World Vision Rwanda was able to integrate 337 women and 253 youth in the honey value chain while in the tailoring value chain 1,752 women and 1,132 youth had been integrated. The final evaluation does underline that there is weak indication of how this integration lead to the increase in trading values as per approved indicator
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
